name: Calophase-44
description: A microencapsulated phase-change material composite manufactured by Crucible Industries, embedding a refined paraffin-salt eutectic blend within a rigid aerogel-ceramic matrix that provides structural integrity while the PCM cores cycle between solid and liquid states to absorb and release latent heat. Calophase-44 maintains interface temperatures within a ±2°C band across its rated operating range of -20°C to 85°C, making it invaluable for thermal buffering in environments with extreme fluctuations. The material is passive and requires no power input.
applications: habitat wall panels in extreme climates
story_hooks: A Calophase-44 panel pulled from a disaster site has locked solid at an anomalous temperature — it absorbed heat from something far outside its rated range, suggesting an unauthorized energy weapon discharge.
Shelf-level communities use scavenged Calophase-44 panels as the only thing standing between their hab-blocks and lethal temperature swings — when a supply is stolen, lives are at immediate risk.
A body is found perfectly preserved inside a Calophase-44 insulated container — the thermal buffering kept the environment stable enough to confuse time-of-death calculations by weeks.
